w: Before his morning worship, Swamishri went for Thakorji’s darshan and the Smruti-Mandir of Shastriji Maharaj. While circumambulating the mandir, a group of 16 devotees and 5 sadhus from Surat were effervescently chanting the Swaminarayan dhun. They had accomplished on foot their pilgrimage of 375 kms from Surat. Swamishri welcomed them by showering rose petals and said, "Sahajanand Swami Maharaj ni jay. The group of devotees from Surat have accomplished their pilgrimage on foot. Maharaj, Swami, Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj are extremely pleased by your effort and devotion. For every step you have attained the fruit of countless Ashwamedh yagnas because you had remembered God and His holy sadhu. You have pilgrimaged by foot to Akshardham!..."
Using paper, styrofoam and cloth, a beautiful stage was created by the sadhus, parshads and sadhaks of Sarangpur.

The birthday celebration of Bhagatji Maharaj commenced in the morning with the singing of dhun and prayer. In his blessings Swamishri said, "Bhagatji Maharaj was born in Mahuva on this very day. Since his birth, he was born to continue the mission of Maharaj. He was wedded to service and attached to Satsang from the beginning... He had developed a strong bond with Gunatitanand Swami - believing him to be the form of Maharaj and that Shriji Maharaj was working through him. Bhagatji Maharaj talked openly about the glory of Shriji Maharaj and Gunatitanand Swami in Junagadh..."
After lunch, at 1.05 p.m., Swamishri blessed a group of 30 devotees who had walked their way from Radhu.
In the evening Swamishri attended a special dramatic performance of 'Karna's Enigma', performed by the children and youth members of the Sanstha.
In the evening assembly, Swamishri chanted the Swaminarayan dhun for peace to prevail in the spate of communal violence in Gujarat.
Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of murtis for a new Swaminarayan Sanskardham in the village of Ramangamadi district Vadodara.

From 6.10 p.m., Swamishri attended the 20th annual day celebration day of Shri Akshar Purushottam Chhatralay. After speeches and bhajans by the chhatralay students a youth performed a monoacting on 'Pibek's Defeat.' The hostel youths performed a drama called 'The Darbar of Dharmaraja' that conveyed the message that morality and spirituality are more important than money and power. After another drama 'A Summons for the Witness', which showed different elements responsible for the erosion of character in today's students, Swamishri blessed the assembly, " ... You must first be conscious that you are students. Your priority is to study and to develop character. You should overcome whatever faults you have. By looking at another's fault you can never improve yourself... The change should be inspired within yourself."

On the way from Junagadh to Gondal, Swamishri visited Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Jetpur for darshan. It was here that Ramanand Swami had appointed the 21-year-old Shriji Maharaj as his successor and head of the Sampraday. ( see photo story )
During Swamishri's stay in Mumbai, on various occasions the children too kept offering their devotion in many ways, from vows and austerities onwards, to please their beloved Swamishri.

Today some young children, Mayur Shashikant Patel (Chicago), Markand Soni, Jogi Dave and Ashish Mehta, had on their own prepared a small skit. Mayur acted out Gunatitanand Swami's saying, 'Sweets made of poison taste good while eating, but a moment later the throat is gripped...', and the other three children choked and fell to the ground as if they had eaten poison and died.
Laughing, Swamishri said, "What does sweets of poison mean?"
The children said nothing.
So Swamishri said, "It means food from the market. So do not eat outside food, and keep your rules and dharma properly."

On Mahashivratri, while Swamishri was doing darshan of Thakorji, a boy, Mumukshu Ajmera, was singing the kirtan 'Yogijine vandan varamvar...'. In it he sang, 'To give moksha to the seekers you travel morning and evening...'
Hearing this, Swamishri said, "He travels day and night only to give moksha to the seekers." Then he added, "To receive moksha, stop eating outside food and listening to outside songs."

On Vasant Panchami, after darshan of Thakorji in the mandir, when Swamishri came to the fifth floor for his morning puja, the kirtan 'Ek ratre...' from the life story of Shastriji Maharaj began. Dressed as the young devotee Dungar Bhakta, Markand Soni walked fearlessly with a stick, turning round and round. The sounds of ghosts came from the background, and soon the masked ghosts all crowded in together. Their attempt to frighten Dungar Bhakta failed. The scene was acted out briefly and won Swamishri's pleasure. Swamishri blessed Markand and all the youths and teenagers who had played the ghosts. Markand said, "Like these ghosts, there are ghosts of maya inside us. Please drive them out."
Swamishri said, "They will surely go." Giving this promise, Swamishri went to his morning puja.
Swamishri easily planted rules of pure food and conduct and high spiritual values in the hearts of the little children.
At 6.10 p.m. Swamishri left New Delhi and arrived in Bhavnagar at 7.20 p.m. Swamishri was welcomed with garlands.

The Pushpadolotsav (Fuldol festival) commenced at 5.00 p.m. After singing of dhun and prayer, senior sadhus discoursed to the mammoth assembly. In conclusion, Swamishri blessed the gathering and showered sanctified coloured water on everyone. (For details and photos see Swaminarayan Bliss, April 2010, p. 23 and back cover).

ds.t: If I protect them, will I not protect myself?
w: Today was the Pushpadol festival. Swamishri was busy from morning. Today Swamishri gave personal meetings to about 175 devotees, and more than 80,000 devotees had begun arriving from morning to enjoy the festival. On such an occasion Swamishri too felt that the sooner he reached the festival, the better.
And so, as Swamishri was going for his afternoon rest, Dr. Kiranbhai Doshi asked him, "The time to reach the assembly is 6:00 in the evening. Do you want to walk this evening?"
"We will see." Saying this Swamishri cut the talk short, but then said, "It is fine to skip it for one day, isn't it!"
Dr. Kiranbhai said, "If there is tension about going to the assembly even while walking, the blood pressure would rise for nothing. What you say is better."

Swamishri said nothing more, but from 4:30 in the evening he sat insisting on going to the assembly. The weather had suddenly turned and it was extremely hot, so it was wise for Swamishri not to go out yet. Even so, Swamishri was firm. While reading letters, Swamishri kept speaking again and again of going to the assembly. So, keeping Swamishri's health in mind, Dr. Kiranbhai said, "The sun outside is very strong."
Looking at the window, Swamishri said calmly, "I can see it too."
Dr. Kiranbhai Doshi said, "It is just as hot outside."
Swamishri said slowly, "What must be happening to those sitting in the assembly?!"
Dr. Kiranbhai said, "They all feel the heat, but since you are there, you will surely protect them!"
Swamishri said, "If I protect them, will I not protect myself?"

Hearing this, Dr. Kiranbhai could say nothing and stayed silent. So Swamishri said again, "The bodies of those sitting in the assembly are not made of iron or wood! They must be feeling the heat too! They are all sitting there with faith, so what harm can come to us?"
In the end, knowing Swamishri's wish, no one said anything.

Seeing the decorated car outside for going to the Pushpadol festival, Swamishri said, "There is no need at all to decorate the car like this. What is the decoration for? It does not suit a sadhu at all, so do not do it. For us sadhus, the simpler the better. There is no need for decoration."
This is Swamishri's constant preference.
